text:
Now the miner (runs the python mathgen, verifies scraped sources against firecrawl fixtures/live content, assembles the candidate), the draft writer, feedback drafter, pipeline, and CLI.

miner.ts:
- runAnalysis(spec, csvPath, cwd): spawn python3 python/mathgen.py analyze --spec tmp --csv out; parse stdout JSON. tmp spec file in runs dir (gitignored) or os tmp.
- verifySources(spec, firecrawl): for links with access "scraped": scrape → check expectations. Expectations: use spec.figures-derived tokens? Simplest robust check: for each scraped link, required substrings (or die). I'll add a `verifyExpect` map in the miner per URL — better: since these fixtures are tied to the mock, define REQUIRED_SUBSTRINGS: Record<url, string[]> in miner or firecrawl client. Simpler: link["expect"]?: string[]. Add to SourceLink type via optional field... The type doesn't have it. I'll handle verification lightly: check markdown non-empty and contains a couple of numeric tokens from the headline. Hmm. Let me do it properly: add optional `expect: string[]` to SourceLink and put 2-3 substrings per scraped link. That's clean.

Update types.ts SourceLink and specs for scraped links (5 of them: destatis, bk de, bk fr, srg, electografia, fide, go.dev (scraped), datatracker is api-json).

Verification semantics: in mock, fixture must contain expect substrings (proves draft claims match "source content"); in live, scraped markdown must contain them (proves the claim is currently verifiable). If missing → reject candidate as unverifiable.

miner.assemble(spec, market): compute signature (sha256 of market|headline|figures), stance = derived after analysis: implied > marketOdds.yes → "yes" else "no". Candidate(EvidenceCandidate) needs signature → assemble after analysis runs. So signatureFor in gate is redundant; candidate gets signature at assembly.

Flow: pipeline: for each eligible market with spec: check dedupe pre-mine: signature computable from spec (headline+figures) without analysis → cheap skip before running python. Then mine: verify sources → run analysis → build candidate → gate → draft → log.

draft.ts: writeDraft(candidate, market, cfg, runTs): build note text, manifest, paths; return DraftOutcome {dir, notePath, csvPath, noteText}. Note text = the 4-part format. The CSV written by python. Manifest json. 

feedback.ts: draftFeedback(run report, cfg, warnings): write drafts/feedback/*.md files: each with a ready JSON body + curl example (draft only, no send). Generate from: (a) restricted-tier warning observation, (b) pots units ambiguity in markets.json, (c) any gate rejects of type "unverifiable" if any. Keep 2-3 static-ish observations encoded as templates.

pipeline.ts: orchestrates; returns RunReport and writes drafts/index.json (latest run report array?) and drafts/SKIPPED.md maybe. Write report to drafts/run-<ts>.json? The brief says drafts ready for QA — indexes: drafts/index.json (map per draft). I'll write:
- drafts/index.json: {generatedAt, runId, drafts: [{topic, dir, market, stance, implied, marketOdds, cutoff}...], skips...} (latest run)
- per-draft note.md/data.csv/manifest.json

CLI: parse args minimally (no dep): commands run/plan; flags --mode=mock|live, --live-submit, --json.

Now write miner.ts.

- destatis: ["118,4", "+2,6 %", "30. November 2026"] — fixture says "VPI Oktober 2026: +2,6 % ... Indexstand 118,4" and "Veröffentlichung der Vorkorrektur am 30. November 2026". Good.

- go.dev: ["released November 12, 2026", "14 open"] — fixture lists "- go1.27.4 (released November 12, 2026)" and "go1.27.5 carries 14 open milestone blockers (14 open / 87 closed..." Good.
